title: Smooth algebraic spaces lift affine first order tests
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], where smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], so its defining ideal sheaf has square zero. Given morphisms $a_0:T_0\to X$ and $b:T\to Y$ over $S$ with $f\circ a_0=b\circ j$, there exists a morphism $a:T\to X$ over $S$ satisfying $f\circ a=b$ and $a\circ j=a_0$. No separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), implication (1) to (2), with definition-formally-smooth (Tag 060G): global lifting for affine first order test thickenings.

proof.text: Smoothness implies local finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to the space map $f$ (space maps are representable by spaces). Apply [lem-sfb-space-infinitesimal-lift-pseudotorsor] to $f,j,a_0,b$. It supplies the quasi-coherent Zariski module $H$ on $T$, the sheaf $\mathcal L$ of the specified lifts on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and its simply transitive $H_{\mathrm{et}}$-action wherever a lift exists. At this point no existence has been inferred from the action.

source.place: Tag 04AM, definition of the sheaf of lifts and translation module; Tags 061A, 061C, 061D

proof.text: Form $Z=X\times_YT$, with projection $p:Z\to T$, and $c_0=(a_0,j):T_0\to Z$. The fibre product exists as an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The arbitrary-base-change law in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] makes $p$ smooth. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme chart $q:U\to Z$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The same calculus says that $q$ is smooth and that $p q:U\to T$ is smooth, now a morphism of schemes. Its scheme formal smoothness is therefore available from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Pull back $q$ along $c_0$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $W_0=T_0\times_ZU\to T_0$ is a surjective etale morphism of schemes, with a specified map $r_0:W_0\to U$ over $T$. By [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site], there is an etale scheme $W\to T$ and an isomorphism $W\times_TT_0\cong W_0$ over $T_0$; the covering condition is preserved, so $W\to T$ is surjective. Choose an affine open cover $\{W_i\}$ of $W$. These are etale over $T$ and jointly cover it. Set $W_{i0}=W_i\times_TT_0$ and restrict $r_0$ through the displayed isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04AM, part (I), expanded using the etale-cover lifting argument in Tag 04CY (lemma-etale-on-top), (4)

proof.text: Each $W_{i0}\hookrightarrow W_i$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes: on $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the pullback of the defining ideal of $j$ generates an ideal $J\subseteq A$ and $J^2=0$, since a product of two generators comes from $\mathcal I^2=0$. The closed subscheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. Apply scheme formal smoothness of $p q:U\to T$ from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] to $r_0|_{W_{i0}}:W_{i0}\to U$ and $W_i\to T$. This gives $r_i:W_i\to U$ over $T$ restricting to $r_0$. The composite $a_i:W_i\xrightarrow{r_i}U\xrightarrow{q}Z\to X$ satisfies $fa_i=b|_{W_i}$ because $p q r_i$ is the structural map to $T$; on $W_{i0}$ it equals $a_0$ because $q r_0=c_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$. Thus $a_i\in\mathcal L(W_i)$.

source.place: Tag 04AM, part (I), scheme formal smoothness on affine members of the lifted etale cover

proof.text: The covering and sections just constructed make $\mathcal L$ locally nonempty. Together with the simply transitive action from [lem-sfb-space-infinitesimal-lift-pseudotorsor], they identify $\mathcal L$ as an $H_{\mathrm{et}}$-torsor in the precise sense of [def-sc-gm-torsor]. The module $H$ is quasi-coherent and $T$ is affine, so [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] with $q=1$ gives $H^1(T_{\mathrm{et}},H_{\mathrm{et}})=0$. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1], the isomorphism class of $\mathcal L$ is the zero class and $\mathcal L$ is isomorphic to the trivial torsor $H_{\mathrm{et}}$. The image of its global zero section is an element $a\in\mathcal L(T)$. By the defining formula for $\mathcal L$, it is an $S$-morphism $T\to X$ with $fa=b$ and $a j=a_0$. The argument has used no separatedness or quasi-compactness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 04AM, part (II); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AJ; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03P2 and coherent.tex Tag 01XB

proof_origin.place: Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), smooth implies formally smooth, torsor argument (I) and (II)

split_report.summary: Followed the Stacks 04AM derivation-torsor proof, making etale-local lifts explicitly through a smooth scheme chart and a lifted cover.
